content: In draft PR #40495, the simpNF linter causes failure in a lot of files that re not related to the one being added, which adds no simp lemmas. When the newly added file is not imported by Mathlib.lean, the simpNF linter does not throw errors. How could a file that the other files don't import and which doesn't introduce any simp lemmas cause the simpNF linter to fail, and how can I debug this?
FWIW you can try lake exe runLinter locally which might repro the failure, though at first glance I don't see what's wrong
Running that immediately gives an error that it failed to read file Mathlib.olean, "incompatible header"
I've commented out the content of the file I'm adding, and I plan to un-comment declarations one at a time, running CI each time, to try to figure out which declaration is causing the problem
I think your current run will fail on @[expose] public section complaining that there are no declarations to expose or make public
I figured out the issue: I made DecidableEq X a global instance instead of constructing it in each proof as necessary and using open scoped Classical in on terms that required it.

Yeah there's a delicate dance to be played around decidability. I've not looked at the code at all but am wondering why you would want decidability at all. There are parts of the library where we're actively trying to remove it.

In this case, I needed DecidableEq X to be able to use the lemma docs#Finset.sum_eq_sum_sdiff_singleton_add, and I needed DecidableRel (G.Adj)to be able to define a piecewise function based on whether vertices of the graph are adjacent. That is, I couldn't even write if G.Adj x y then 1 else 0 without an instance of DecidableRel (G.Adj).
Edit: it was also necessary to be able to write set differences like: univ \ {x}.
Well you could always use docs#finsum for the first thing, but for the second yeah you probably have to be careful.
